analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) Connecting You to GS, 2) Credit Update, 3) Hungary Fiscal Plan Today, 4) CXMT 4F2 Implications and 5) Week Ahead Previews 19 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS Chief US Economist David Mericle does not think the October FOMC meeting is live after the CPI print. Williams, Jefferson, Daly and Chairman Warsh have all signaled an every-other-meeting pace, so GS expects a pause in October, a second hike in December that is the last one, and cuts once inflation nears 2% in the back half of next year.
GS views are more dovish than market pricing, which has the funds rate staying above 4.5% over the next couple of years.

GS Treasury trading (Brandon Brown) sees the Fed skipping October, with 4.5bp priced for that meeting and 22bp priced for December. He calls the market's high confidence in a December hike a little surprising and describes Fed messaging as confusing.

GS FX strategy (Mike Cahill) notes Governor Waller said the Fed's pushback was a coordinated effort to walk back October pricing. The Fed's path is one more hike this year, with mixed views on adding another in 2027.

GS credit strategy (Amanda Lynam): higher rates have raised questions about AI capex funding, and the impact is largest in USD HY. GS stays underweight USD IG Technology and neutral USD HY, seeing scope for a near-term reversal of the recent sell-off, with dispersion across AI-related issuers likely to stay high.
USD IG and HY project finance issuance year to date has passed $106B, nearly triple the $37B in 2025. Risks to the GS 2027 global forecast of $300B are skewed firmly to the upside.

GS IG cash trading (Brad Shelofsky): credit and equities have diverged all year. Equities are near all-time highs on the largest AI names, while IG and HY indexes sit in the 10th and 20th percentile, and hyperscaler and data centre baskets are near all-time wides. HY project finance bonds trade around $94, down from $101 in the summer.

Shelofsky says high-beta HY weakness reflects tests of neocloud and data centre financing in a higher-for-longer rate world, plus technicals after the two largest HY deals in history pushed HY net risk to a two-year high.

Shelofsky says hyperscaler issuance has not plateaued, with visibility probably a mid-2027 conversation. The hyperscaler basket is 70bp cheap to the broader market at the wides in yield, and he calls the setup into year end constructive. Chip financing could test concentration-risk discounts in early 2027.

Hungary PM Peter Magyar presents the 2027 budget and medium-term fiscal plan at 1pm local time. GS expects a 2027 deficit of 5% versus 7.5% this year, and 3% by 2029, implying ERM II in mid-2028 and euro adoption in January 2031.

GS market strategy (Vitali Meschoulam) says expectations for Hungary improved after the IMF meetings. The consensus 2027 deficit is now near 5.3%, so a deficit above 5.5% would disappoint and a 4-handle would be a meaningful positive surprise. HUF outperformed and HUF rates fell versus EUR last week.

GS equity research (Lee): memory suppliers (Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Micron, SanDisk, Kioxia, CXMT) fell 11-26%, erasing about $738B in market value, after CXMT's Oct 10 disclosure of a '4F2' DRAM cell architecture with a server-memory product planned by end-2026.

GS attributes part of the memory sell-off to other factors: credit and AI financing concerns and the higher CPI. CXMT itself declined, NAND names less exposed also sold off, and DRAM spot prices kept rising.

GS says a significant technology gap remains for CXMT in advanced-node DRAM and HBM. The market may have underestimated CXMT's capacity ramp but overestimated the pace of a technology breakthrough, given customer qualification and high-yield mass production timelines.

Samsung Electronics trades at 1.2x/0.9x and SK Hynix at 1.4x/0.9x P/B for 2027E/2028E, which GS says prices a 2028 downcycle, more pessimistic than GS's higher-for-longer view. GS sees attractive risk/reward but limited near-term catalysts.

Week ahead: MNB Tuesday (GS and consensus hold at 5.50%), UK labor data Tuesday, UK core CPI Wednesday (GS 2.8% vs consensus 2.7%), Tesla, Meta and IBM earnings Wednesday, CBRT Thursday (GS hold at 37.0% vs consensus 100bp cut, with risks skewed to a small cut), US flash manufacturing PMI Friday.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees attractive risk/reward after the CXMT-driven sell-off. The stock trades at 1.2x 2027E P/B and 0.9x 2028E P/B, below book, which prices a 2028 downcycle.
SK Hynix trades at 1.4x 2027E P/B and 0.9x 2028E P/B. GS sees a significant technology gap vs CXMT in advanced DRAM and HBM, and near-term catalysts are limited.
